Sample more chains for a fitted model

Source: R/add_chains.R
add_chains.Rd

add_chains() samples more chains of a model fitted with bmm() and returns one fit with the chains of fit followed by the new ones. Use it when a fit needs more draws, for example because its effective sample sizes are too small, and the chains it has should be kept.

Usage

add_chains(fit, chains = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

A bmmfit object sampled with MCMC (algorithm = "sampling") by the rstan or cmdstanr backend.

chains

The number of chains to add, a positive whole number.

seed

The seed of the new chains. If NULL (the default), a seed is drawn from R's random number generator. bmm draws the default initial values from R's random number generator too, so call set.seed() before add_chains() to make the new chains reproducible, with or without seed. A seed that a chain of fit was sampled with is refused, because the new chains could repeat that chain's draws.

...

Further arguments passed to update.bmmfit(), such as cores, refresh or control. threads works only for a fit that was sampled with threading, because a threaded Stan program differs from an unthreaded one. Arguments that would change the model, the data, the draws per chain or what is sampled (formula., newdata, data, data2, model, prior, sample_prior, iter, warmup, thin, algorithm, backend and normalize) are refused: use update() for those and sample all chains anew. file and file_compress are refused too; save the result with saveRDS().

Value

A bmmfit object with the chains of fit followed by the new ones, combined with brms::combine_models(). Everything else is taken from fit, except criteria added with brms::add_criterion(): they were computed from the chains of fit alone and are removed, so add them again. The result has no file, so brms::add_criterion() does not write it over the file of fit. version and the other fields that describe the fit are those of fit; the new chains ran the same Stan program. fit_info() reports the time, step size and inverse metric of every chain.

Details

The new chains are sampled with update(), which recompiles the Stan model only when it needs to, for example for a cmdstanr fit loaded in a new R session. If the Stan program that bmm now writes for the model differs from the one fit was sampled with, as it can after an update of bmm or brms, the new chains would not sample the same posterior, and add_chains() stops after sampling them. Refit the model with bmm() in that case.

See also

fit_info(), update.bmmfit()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # identical(Sys.getenv("BMM_EXAMPLES"), "true")
fit <- bmm(
  formula = bmmformula(c ~ 1, kappa ~ 1),
  data = data.frame(y = rsdm(1000)),
  model = sdm(resp_error = "y"),
  chains = 2
)

# two more chains, four in all
fit <- add_chains(fit, chains = 2)
fit_info(fit, "time")
}
